concepts.heading: Kink-Informed Care: A Strength-Based Approach
concepts.plain: Good care treats kink as a normal part of sexuality, not a problem to fix.

concepts.heading: A Brief History: Kink and the DSM
concepts.plain: For decades kink was listed as a mental disorder.

concepts.heading: Dr. David Ley's Research
concepts.plain: Research has added a lot to how we understand kink as positive sexuality.

concepts.heading: Kink as Identity vs Activity
concepts.plain: For some people kink is part of who they are. For others it is something they do.

concepts.heading: Midori's Framework
concepts.plain: Kink is a skill you learn step by step, with consent at the centre.

concepts.heading: Non-Shaming Framing
concepts.plain: Being into kink does not mean you are damaged.

checks.after: A Brief History: Kink and the DSM
checks.prompt: How was kink classified for decades?
options: As a mental disorder in the DSM
checks.explanation: As a mental disorder in the DSM. For decades, kink and BDSM interests were classified as mental disorders in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual (DSM).
A healthy expression of sexuality. Exploring kink is a healthy expression of sexuality, not a sign of trauma or dysfunction.

2bbeb7b9-984f-488e-a367-f29b14496fc4.takeaway: Kink between consenting adults is a healthy part of sexuality, not a disorder.

concepts.heading: Consent Frameworks: SSC, RACK, & PRICK
concepts.plain: Kink communities have built some of the most careful consent systems anywhere.

concepts.heading: SSC: Safe, Sane, Consensual
concepts.plain: SSC means safe, sane and consensual. It is the oldest of these systems.

concepts.heading: RACK: Risk-Aware Consensual Kink
concepts.plain: RACK means risk-aware consensual kink. It came after SSC to cover its gaps.

concepts.heading: PRICK: Personal Responsibility, Informed Consensual Kink
concepts.plain: PRICK adds personal responsibility: each person owns their choices.

concepts.heading: Comparing the Frameworks
concepts.plain: No one system is right for everyone. Use what fits.

concepts.heading: Connection to the FRIES Model
concepts.plain: All of these connect back to FRIES from the first badge.

checks.explanation: Safe, Sane, Consensual. SSC stands for Safe, Sane, Consensual. It is the oldest and most widely known kink consent framework.
Risk-Aware Consensual Kink. RACK stands for Risk-Aware Consensual Kink. It emerged as a response to SSC's limitations.

46e99fcb-18ba-4860-b549-8bf141178f3a.takeaway: Kink communities built careful consent systems. All of them rest on informed, willing agreement.

concepts.heading: Scene Negotiation & Communication
concepts.plain: A scene is a planned activity with a set time, place and limits.

concepts.heading: The Negotiation Process
concepts.plain: Talk it all through before you begin.

concepts.heading: Key Negotiation Elements
concepts.plain: Start with exactly what is on the table and what is not.

concepts.heading: Ongoing Negotiation
concepts.plain: Keep checking in once you have started. Consent does not end at the start.

concepts.heading: The Power of "No"
concepts.plain: The person receiving has the final say. They can stop anything at any time.

concepts.heading: Negotiation in ENM
concepts.plain: With several partners, make sure everyone affected knows what they need to know.

checks.explanation: Before play begins. Scene negotiation happens before play begins. It is a structured conversation where all participants discuss desires, limits, logistics, and safety protocols.

checks.prompt: Who holds the most power in a healthy kink dynamic?
options: The bottom or submissive, who can stop any activity
checks.explanation: The bottom or submissive, who can stop any activity. The bottom or submissive ultimately holds the most power through their ability to stop any activity.

c9d7b84f-15d2-4d0e-9fff-21978a4290d4.takeaway: Agree on everything before you start, keep checking in, and "no" always wins.

concepts.heading: Aftercare & Ongoing Wellbeing
concepts.plain: Aftercare is the time you spend looking after each other afterwards.

concepts.heading: Physical Aftercare
concepts.plain: Bodies need looking after, starting with water or a warm drink.

concepts.heading: Emotional Aftercare
concepts.plain: Hearts need reassurance and kind words.

concepts.heading: Aftercare Is Ongoing
concepts.plain: Check in again later. Feelings can keep coming up after it is over.

concepts.heading: When Kink Brings Up the Unexpected
concepts.plain: If something unexpected comes up, like an old memory, slow down and get support.

concepts.heading: Ongoing Kink Education
concepts.plain: Keep learning. Good practice is never finished.

options: The period of care, connection and recovery following a scene
checks.explanation: The period of care, connection and recovery following a scene. Aftercare is the period of care, connection, and recovery following a kink scene.

checks.prompt: Does emotional processing always end right after the scene?
options: No, it can continue well beyond
checks.explanation: No, it can continue well beyond. Sometimes emotional processing continues well beyond the immediate post-scene period.

ed73aa73-4dd8-4d31-95a6-3118a1c4f3e8.takeaway: After something intense, look after each other: water, warmth, kind words, and a check-in later.
